We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx rates and tail latency for inference calls to model: redwood/llama-13b on our EU instances around 10:50 ET. Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to ~6% and p99 token latency jumped from ~180ms to ~1.8s. The failures look like a mix of 502/504 and some connection timeouts.

We've attached a short trace and a few request IDs. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side or our peering? Engineers are seeing spikes across several AZs.

— Aisha (Lynx Ops)

Looping in network. Early note: Dedicated peered VPC customers occasionally hit transient NAT exhaustion during short bursts, which can manifest as 502/504 and timeouts at the edge. Jonas, can you check NAT conntrack and proxy queue lengths for Lynx's pools between 10:30–11:15 ET?

Also, can infra confirm whether our resolver for that peer flip-flopped to a fallback that adds an extra hop? That would explain p99 token jump.

Rishi
Head of Reliability

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2026 13:25:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: production errors and latency spike

Quick analysis from edge and peering logs (10:40–11:05 ET):
- Observed burst of SYN retransmits from Lynx's peer ASN to our egress proxy, correlated with increased session drops on SNAT pool 12 in eu-west-1.
- Resolver switch noted: queries that previously hit resolver-a (50ms median) retried to resolver-b (400ms median) for ~9 minutes starting 10:47 ET.
- Proxy reported 503 due to backend connection timeouts when retrying across the slower resolver path.

I attached a trimmed traceroute and a zipped set of proxy logs showing repeated DNS NXDOMAIN->retry sequences. Looks like the peering path introduced added RTT and some connection churn to the proxy layer.

Attachments: lynx-trace-1105.txt, lynx-proxy-logs-1105.zip

I recommend: 1) short-term: fail traffic to an alternate peering path or enable direct dedicated route via fastpath; 2) mid-term: increase SNAT pool and tune conntrack timeouts for this customer; 3) continue debugging resolver health on peer.

— Jonas (Network Ops)

Subject: RE: production errors and latency spike — summary & next steps

Aisha / team —

Thank you again for the quick artifacts. Summary from our side: between 10:47–10:56 ET an unexpected resolver failover coincided with elevated retransmits on the peering path which temporarily reduced available SNAT slots for your Dedicated pool, causing retries that surfaced as 502/504 and higher p99 token latency.

What we're doing now (timeline):
- 18:20 ET: completed failover to alternate peering path (traffic shift validated) — immediate p99 improvement observed in monitoring
- 18:35 ET: expanded SNAT pool for your Dedicated tenant (reduces conntrack collisions) — pushing new conntrack thresholds to prod
- 19:00 ET: our network team will run a stability test and keep hourly check-ins for 6 hours

Customer-facing ask: please confirm whether you want a follow-up call at 19:15 ET for a live walk-through of traces. We propose a one-time credit for the 10:45–11:15 ET window; Marissa will propose language.

We'll keep this open and send an incident postmortem within 48 hours with root cause and permanent mitigations (resolver pinning and SNAT pool autoscaling for affected Dedicated tenants).

Diego Fernandez
